title: Best Cheap GPS Watches for Running
excerpt: The best budget GPS running watches by list price: Coros Pace 4, Garmin Forerunner 70 and Fitbit Charge 6, with battery and feature trade-offs.
body:
Best Cheap GPS Watches for Running

Updated November 2026. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update; retailers often sell for less.

A capable GPS running watch now has a list price of about $250. Below that, you're mostly looking at fitness bands with built-in GPS. They track distance well enough for easy runs but are less dependable for pacing workouts. This guide compares the best budget options by list price (MSRP), using each maker's specs and published reviews. Retailers often discount these watches.

The picks

Coros Pace 4: most battery for the money

The Coros Pace 4 lists at $249. It's rated for 41 hours of standard GPS, or 31 hours in dual-band mode. That's enough for a few weeks of normal training between charges. The Coros Pace 4 has an AMOLED display and weighs 32 g with its nylon band. It can also play MP3 files you load yourself, but it doesn't support Spotify or other streaming services.

Garmin Forerunner 70: simplest Garmin

The Garmin Forerunner 70 lists at $249.99. It's rated for 23 hours in GPS-only mode and 13 days as a smartwatch. It has an AMOLED screen and works with Garmin's training app. It uses multi-GNSS rather than the multi-band GPS on Garmin's pricier watches, and it has no music storage.

Fitbit Charge 6: cheapest built-in GPS

The Fitbit Charge 6 lists at $159.95. It's a fitness band with built-in GPS, rated for up to 7 days of general use, which drops when you use GPS. Reviewers found its built-in GPS less reliable than a dedicated running watch's. It's fine for logging easy runs, but not for precise pacing.

If you can stretch: Garmin Forerunner 170

The Garmin Forerunner 170 lists at $299.99 and is rated for 20 hours in GPS-only mode. It adds features such as contactless payment over the Forerunner 70. The Forerunner 170 Music version lists at $349.99 and stores offline playlists from Spotify, Amazon Music and Deezer.

What you give up at the budget end

  • Multi-band GPS: this is missing from the cheaper Garmins. The Coros Pace 4 is the exception at this price.
  • Offline maps: these usually start at higher prices. The Coros Pace 4 has added them.
  • Streaming music: on Garmin, you need a "Music" model.

How to choose

  • Training for a specific race, or running more than three times a week: buy a dedicated running watch, such as the Coros Pace 4 or Garmin Forerunner 70.
  • Running casually and mainly wanting distance and rough pace: a Fitbit Charge 6, or your phone, may be enough.
  • Battery is the priority: Coros Pace 4.
  • You want Garmin's app: Forerunner 70.

FAQ

What is the cheapest good GPS running watch?

By list price, the Coros Pace 4 and the Garmin Forerunner 70 are the cheapest dedicated running watches covered here. The Coros Pace 4 lists at $249. The Garmin Forerunner 70 lists at $249.99. Discounts are common, so compare the current price with the list price.

Do cheap GPS watches measure distance accurately?

Dedicated running watches are accurate enough for training. Fitness bands with built-in GPS, such as the Fitbit Charge 6, are less consistent, according to reviewers.
